title: Stop Saying 'Very'! 50 Stronger Words Every Intermediate English Learner Should Know
dek: Level up your English vocabulary by replacing repetitive 'very + adjective' combinations with 50 powerful, precise adjectives and bonus advanced upgrades.

blocks.say: One of the most noticeable signs of the intermediate plateau is relying on 'very' to intensify everyday words. Transitioning to stronger single-word adjectives makes your English vivid and concise.

blocks.text: While saying 'very big' or 'very good' is grammatically correct, overusing 'very' sounds repetitive. Strong single-word adjectives make your spoken and written communication express emotions with precision.
blocks.say: Strong single-word adjectives make your spoken and written communication express emotions with precision.
Here are key adjective upgrades for everyday conversations.

blocks.targetText: I had a hectic day at work and I am completely exhausted.
blocks.say: I had a hectic day at work and I am completely exhausted.

blocks.targetText: The view from the mountain peak was breathtaking.
blocks.say: The view from the mountain peak was breathtaking.
Say It section. Practice stress on strong multi-syllable adjectives.

blocks.title: Extreme Adjectives Don't Take 'Very'
blocks.content: Strong adjectives like 'exhausted', 'freezing', or 'spotless' already include 'very' in their definition. Instead of 'very freezing', native speakers say 'completely freezing' or 'absolutely spotless'.
blocks.say: Culture bite: Strong adjectives take 'absolutely' or 'completely' instead of 'very'.
